checkpoint_text:
Step 1: Convert the time taken to travel 1 kilometer from hours to seconds.
1 hour = 3600 seconds, so 2.5 hours = 2.5 * 3600 seconds.

Step 2: Calculate the speed of the robot in meters per second.
Since the robot travels 1000 meters (1 kilometer) in 2.5 * 3600 seconds, its speed is \( \frac{1000}{2.5 \times 3600} \) meters per second.

Step 3: Use the speed calculated in Step 2 to find the length of the hallway.
The robot takes 90 seconds to travel the length of the hallway. Using the speed found in Step 2, the length of the hallway is \( \text{speed} \times 90 \).

Step 4: Substitute the speed into the equation for the length of the hallway.
\[ \text{Length of the hallway} = \left( \frac{1000}{2.5 \times 3600} \right) \times 90 \]

Step 5: Simplify the expression.
\[ \text{Length of the hallway} = \left( \frac{1000}{9000} \right) \times 90 = \frac{1}{9} \times 90 = 10 \text{ meters} \]

Final answer: \boxed{10}
